newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SOCCER-BROLIN FACING UP TO RETURN TO LEEDS - PAPERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BROLIN FACING UP TO RETURN TO LEEDS - PAPERS.

text.p: Swedish striker Tomas Brolin is facing up to a return to English club Leeds where he had a chequered spell 18 months ago, Swedish newspapers said on Thursday.
After a season on loan to Italy's Parma, Brolin said he had no choice but to go back to Leeds where he still has another year on his contract.
"If I must play at Leeds then I will," Brolin told newspaper Expressen. "If Leeds is now the only alternative then I must accept that."
Brolin was taken on for a fee of 4.5 million pounds ($7.4 million) by former manager Howard Wilkinson in November 1995.
The Swede played only 24 games for Leeds and scored four goals. He fell out with Wilkinson and left under a shower of criticism from fans when he was loaned back to former club Parma.
Brolin said he had not kept in touch with the other players at Leeds nor the board.
"But I have spoken with my agent (John Smith) and we came to the conclusion that it is best if I do (return). I don't think I will have any problem with (manager George) Graham now."
Brolin told another tabloid, Aftonbladet. "We have a lot of things to sort out at a meeting on Tuesday."
